question: A causal continuous-time rational LTI transfer function has no pole-zero cancellations. Which pole sets imply BIBO stability?

steps: For a causal rational response the ROC lies to the right of its rightmost pole.
BIBO stability requires the imaginary axis in the ROC, which occurs only when all poles are strictly left of it.
A and D qualify; the pole at zero in B and right-half-plane pole in C do not.
solution.explanation: A and D qualify; the pole at zero in B and right-half-plane pole in C do not.
commonMistakes: A pole on the imaginary axis fails the strict BIBO condition.

hints: Identify the conditions under which causal rational stability applies.

Therefore it is BIBO-stable, LTI, and a one-unit advance: C.
